title: 心念处

evidence.pali: 106 . ‘‘Ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā, sokaparidevānaṃ pariddavānaṃ (sī. pī.) samatikkamāya, dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya, ñāyassa adhigamāya, nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 106. 诸比丘，此是唯一之道，为诸有情之清净，为超越愁悲，为灭尽苦忧，为证得正理，为现证涅槃，此即是四念处。
evidence.english: 106. “Bhikkhus, this is the one and only way for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the disappearance of suffering and displeasure, for the attainment of the noble path, for the realization of Nibbāna—namely, the four establishments of mindfulness.”

isolation_reason: 旧图保留的独立概念有直接 V4 逐句证据，但当前闭包没有足够直接的关系句将其连接到另一发布节点；为避免凭概念相似度补边，保留为可检索、可引用的独立节点。

entries.pali: Tattha catūsu…pe… pariññaṃ gacchantī ti kāyāgatāsatipaṭṭhāne yogāvacarena bhāviyamāne sati tena yogāvacarena asubhe kesādike rūpakāye ‘‘subha’’nti vipallāso pahīyati, assa yogāvacarassa kabaḷīkārāhāro pariññaṃ gacchati, ‘‘āhārasamudayā rūpasamudayo’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.56) vuttattā rūpakāye chandarāgaṃ pajahantassa tassa samudaye kabaḷīkārāhārepi chandarāgo pahīyatīti attho. Vedanāgatāsatipaṭṭhāne bhāviyamāne sati dukkhe ‘‘sukha’’nti vipallāso pahīyati, assa yogāvacarassa phassāhāro pariññaṃ gacchati, ‘‘phassapaccayā vedanā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.126; saṃ. ni. 2.1, 39; mahāva. 1; udā. 1; vibha. 225) vuttattā vedanāya chandarāgaṃ pajahantassa tassa paccaye phassāhāre chandarāgo pahīyati. Cittagatāsatipaṭṭhāne bhāviyamāne anicce ‘‘nicca’’nti vipallāso pahīyati, assa yogāvacarassa viññāṇāhāro pariññaṃ gacchati. Dhammagatāsatipaṭṭhāne bhāviyamāne anattani ‘‘attā’’ti vipallāso pahīyati, assa yogāvacarassa manosañcetanāhāro pariññaṃ gacchatīti visuṃ visuṃ yojetvā ekekasmiṃ pahātabbe vutte tadavasesā pahātabbā vuttā bhavanti pahātabbabhāvena ekalakkhaṇattāti attho gahetabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于此，于四念处中……趋于遍知。当行者修习身至念处(kāyāgatāsatipaṭṭhāna)时，他断除对于头发等不净色身作‘净’想的颠倒；他的抟食(kabaḷīkārāhāra)趋于遍知。因为经中说‘由食之集而有色之集’(《相应部》3.56)，义为：当舍弃对色身的欲贪时，对其生起之因的抟食的欲贪也被舍弃。当修习受念处(vedanāgatāsatipaṭṭhāna)时，他断除对苦作‘乐’想的颠倒；他的触食(phassāhāra)趋于遍知。因为经中说‘缘触而有受’(《中部》3.126等)，当舍弃对受的欲贪时，对其缘的触食的欲贪也被舍弃。当修习心念处(cittagatāsatipaṭṭhāna)时，他断除对无常作‘常’想的颠倒；他的识食(viññāṇāhāra)趋于遍知。当修习法念处(dhammagatāsatipaṭṭhāna)时，他断除对无我作‘我’想的颠倒；他的意思食(manosañcetanāhāra)趋于遍知。应如是分别结合：当每一项中一个应断除者被说及时，其余应断除者亦被说及，因为就‘应被断除’而言，它们具有单一特征。此即应领会之义。
entries.english: Therein, 'in the four... etc. ...they go to full understanding' means: when the establishment of mindfulness directed to the body is being developed by a meditator, the perversion of 'beautiful' regarding the foul physical body, beginning with the hair of the head, is abandoned by that meditator. For this meditator, the nutriment of physical food goes to full understanding. Because it is said, 'from the arising of nutriment, there is the arising of form,' the meaning is that for one who abandons sensual desire for the physical body, sensual desire is also abandoned for its origin, the nutriment of physical food. When the establishment of mindfulness directed to feelings is being developed, the perversion of 'pleasant' in what is suffering is abandoned; for this meditator, the nutriment of contact goes to full understanding. Because it is said, 'with contact as condition, feeling arises,' for one who abandons sensual desire for feeling, sensual desire is also abandoned for its condition, the nutriment of contact. When the establishment of mindfulness directed to the mind is being developed, the perversion of 'permanent' in what is impermanent is abandoned; for this meditator, the nutriment of consciousness goes to full understanding. When the establishment of mindfulness directed to phenomena is being developed, the perversion of 'self' in what is not-self is abandoned; for this meditator, the nutriment of mental volition goes to full understanding. The meaning should be understood that, having applied this separately to each, when one thing to be abandoned is mentioned, the remaining things to be abandoned are also stated, because they have a single characteristic in that they are to be abandoned.

entries.pali: Hārakasaddassa bhedato atthaṃ vitthāretvā ubhayampi ekamevāti dassetuṃ ‘‘satthañca taṃ hārakañcā’’ tiādi vuttaṃ. Etena thāvarappayogaṃ dasseti sāhatthikādīsu payogesu. ‘‘Iti cittamano’’ ti uddharitvāpi itisaddassa attho na tāva vutto. Kiñcāpi na vutto, adhikāravasena pana āgataṃ itisaddaṃ yojetvā iti cittasaṅkappo ti ettha ‘‘maraṇasaññī maraṇacetano maraṇādhippāyo’’ti vuttattā maraṇaṃyeva vakkhatīti veditabbo. Vuttanayenā ti chappayogavasena. Sāhatthikanissaggiyappayogesu sanniṭṭhāpakacetanāya sattamāya saha uppannakāyaviññattiyā sāhatthikatā veditabbā. Āṇattike pana sattahipi cetanāhi saha vacīviññattisambhavato satta satta saddā ekato hutvā ekekakkharabhāvaṃ gantvā yattakehi akkharehi attano adhippāyaṃ viññāpenti, tadavasānakkharasamuṭṭhāpikāya sattamacetanāya sahajātavacīviññattiyā āṇattikatā veditabbā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 通过分解‘运送者’（hārakassa），广说其义，为显示二者实为一体，故说‘刀与彼运送者’等。以此于亲手等加行中，显示常住加行。虽引用‘如是心意’，然‘如是’一词之义尚未说明。虽未说明，然依文义，当结合所引之‘如是’一词，于‘如是心念’处，因说‘有死想、有死思、有死之意向’，故应知其唯指死亡。所谓‘已说之理’，即依六种加行。于亲手加行与抛出物加行中，当知亲手性是由与第七决意思俱生之身表而构成。于命令加行中，因语表可与七种思俱起，故诸声合为一体，成一一字，以若干字表明己意，当知命令性是由生起末字之第七思与俱生之语表而构成。
entries.english: Having elaborated the meaning by distinguishing the term 'remover' (hāraka), to show that both are one and the same, the phrase beginning 'the weapon and that remover' was stated. By this, it shows the application of a fixed device in the context of applications such as direct action. Even after quoting 'thus with mind,' the meaning of the word 'iti' has not yet been stated. Although it has not been stated, by connecting the word 'iti' which has come up here by virtue of the topic, with 'thus with mental resolve,' it should be understood that because it is said, 'perceiving death, intending death, having the aim of death,' death itself will be spoken of. 'According to the method stated' means by way of the six applications. In the applications of direct action and relinquishment, direct action should be understood as the bodily intimation arisen together with the seventh, finalizing volition. In the case of a command, however, since vocal intimation can arise with all seven volitions, various sounds, having come together and become single syllables, by as many syllables as they convey one's intention, command should be understood as the vocal intimation co-arisen with the seventh volition which originates the final syllable.
